clue.text: Poles need jobs

definitions.meaning: upright stakes or columns, such as goalposts
positions of employment, as in an advertised vacancy

explanation.surface: Poland's workers are short of employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' poses as the nationality, but it means upright stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: wooden uprights fixed in the ground, and appointments someone holds at work.

clue.text: Causing offence by eviction

definitions.meaning: throwing someone out of their home

explanation.surface: A landlord's eviction notice gives offence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bothering a person and literally ejecting them from a building.

clue.text: Shouted for a mark to be inserted in plaster strip

indicators.note: says the pieces before it go inside the strip named after it

parts.note: a screed is a levelling strip or layer of plaster or mortar
M stands for the mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone yelled because a blemish had to be set into a strip of plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be inserted in' puts A and M inside SCREED. 'mark' looks like a smudge, but it is the German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to cry out loudly in a piercing voice.

clue.text: Walking a short way to an Essex forest

parts.note: a way shortened: ST is the abbreviation for street
Epping Forest is an ancient woodland in Essex, north-east of London

explanation.surface: Someone strolls a little distance to reach a woodland in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: EPPING Forest is a large ancient woodland in the English county of Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving by placing one foot after the other is walking.

clue.text: Weird man is imprisoned by father. That takes some beating

indicators.note: the pieces before it are locked up inside the word after it

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
rum is old British slang for strange or odd
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A strange man is locked up by his father, which is hard to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'is imprisoned by' sets the weird man inside father. 'That takes some beating' sounds like praise but literally describes something struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum's stretched skin is the part struck with sticks, so it literally receives the beating.

clue.text: Accomplished fellow on English

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A gifted man of English birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places DON above E in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accomplished has been finished or completed.

clue.text: Nickel is found in great quantity in Germany

indicators.note: the metal named first sits inside the word that follows

parts.note: much means a large amount
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A metal turns up in abundance in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'is found in' puts the chemical symbol inside the word for a large amount; the definition is a place, 'in Germany'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian capital is a city located in southern Germany.

clue.text: In time a renegade makes mistakes

indicators.note: the traitor sits inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays a cause

explanation.surface: Over time a traitor makes errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'In' sets the traitor inside the period; 'renegade' as a rodent is old slang for a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors listed for correction, the plural of erratum.

clue.text: Drug information

definitions.meaning: cannabis or another narcotic, in slang

explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses one short word for both a narcotic and the latest facts on a subject.

clue.text: Attacked for being under the influence of drugs

definitions.meaning: high or stimulated by a narcotic

explanation.surface: Someone was assaulted because they were high.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to round on someone, and as slang it means aroused or stimulated, as by narcotics.

clue.text: Reckon that the property extends about one mile

indicators.note: the land stretches round the pieces that follow, enclosing them

parts.note: an estate is a landed property
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Guess how far the grounds stretch: roughly a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extends about' puts I and M inside ESTATE. 'about' seems to mean roughly, but it means around.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate roughly or judge an amount.

clue.text: Knocking someone out is most attractive

definitions.meaning: rendering a person unconscious with a blow

explanation.surface: Flooring someone is the best-looking move.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes dazing with a blow and, figuratively, a beauty that dazes the onlooker.

clue.text: Having difficulty travelling to Spain

indicators.note: letters on the move end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller to Spain runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges TO SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in a tricky situation or a fix.

clue.text: Holiday telegram may trigger alarm

parts.note: a trip is a journey taken for pleasure
a wire is an old term for a telegram

explanation.surface: A telegram sent from a holiday might cause panic at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut cord stretched low across a path sets off a device or warning when someone stumbles on it.

clue.text: Rendering by a boisterous group of actors

parts.note: rough means rowdy or violent
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A performance given by a rowdy troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendering' suggests a performance, but it is the builder's coat applied to walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse plaster finish with gravel in it is spread on outside walls, a kind of exterior coating.

clue.text: He nattered incoherently when menaces were uttered

indicators.note: words spoken without order come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A man chattered unintelligibly while threats were being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incoherently' rearranges HE NATTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying that menaces were uttered amounts to saying someone was intimidated with warnings of harm.

clue.text: Poor ales needing to be changed by senior citizen

indicators.note: the letters must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Bad beer has to be swapped by an elderly drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' rearranges POOR ALES NEEDING. 'Poor' is part of the fodder, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person drawing the state retirement benefit is an elderly citizen.

clue.text: Suggesting that I am working steadily

parts.note: contracted to I'm
plying is working at something diligently, as in plying a trade

explanation.surface: Hinting that one is diligent at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinting at something without stating it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: A refusal, for instance, to be taken in by local resident

indicators.note: the abbreviation is received inside the word that follows

parts.note: a native is someone born and living in a place
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A local might reject being fooled, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'to be taken in by' looks like being deceived, but it means one piece is placed inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A no is a response that denies or declines.

clue.text: Drain it to conform to custom

indicators.note: the letters are made to fit a new shape

explanation.surface: Empty it to fit in with the usual practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conform' rearranges DRAIN IT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-established practice handed down is a custom.

clue.text: Skilful presentation of a legal claim

parts.note: droit is a legal right or claim

explanation.surface: A deft way of putting a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous or clever with hands or mind.

clue.text: My skin is not dark enough to pierce

definitions.text: My skin is not dark enough

definitions.meaning: to run through with a spike

explanation.surface: A fair-skinned person complains, then turns to stabbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a phrase split into two words, I'M PALE; the second is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiking through something with a sharp stake is piercing it; the pale-skinned speaker says the split phrase.

clue.text: Blade totally concealed in a French glove

indicators.note: the word for totally is hidden inside the glove

parts.note: gant is French for glove
all means wholly

explanation.surface: A knife is hidden in a French glove.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'concealed in' signals the container. 'Blade' suggests a knife, but it is an old word for a dashing young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a dashing young man about town, as is a gallant.

clue.text: Special constable rebuked and rejected

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
rapped means criticised sharply, as in rapped over the knuckles

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman was reprimanded and dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer officer in British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown out or abandoned has been discarded.

clue.text: Leave out a container for rubbish

definitions.meaning: a large open bin for builders' waste

explanation.surface: Omit a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is the large open metal bin left on a street for building waste.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means to omit and also names the large open builders' bin for waste.

clue.text: English boy returned to the valley

indicators.note: the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: An English lad came back to the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns E plus LAD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: " — should be made of sterner stuff." (Shakespeare, 'Julius Caesar')

definitions.text: " — should be made of sterner stuff." (Shakespeare, 'Julius Caesar')

parts.words: " — should be made of sterner stuff." (Shakespeare, 'Julius Caesar')
parts.note: Mark Antony's funeral speech line about Caesar; the missing word is the quality Brutus charged him with

explanation.surface: A line from Antony's oration over Caesar's body with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony argues that Caesar lacked the hard drive for power, the quality named in the line.

clue.text: Game pate — nice if freshly served

indicators.note: the letters are dished up again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tasty game pâté, if newly brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly served' rearranges PATE and NICE. 'Game' looks like an adjective for the pâté, but it is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire card game played alone is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Acquisitiveness results from a meagre education

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Grasping behaviour stems from poor schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results from' signals the letters are taken from inside MEAGRE EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquisitiveness is the urge to amass things, an excessive desire for more.
